questions.stem: The doctrine that the powers of the State must be subject to specific limits laid down by the Constitution, so as to prevent arbitrary rule, is known as:
Which one of the following is a feature of the parliamentary system of government as adopted in India?
options: The executive is not responsible to the legislature
There is a strict separation of powers between the executive and legislature
The real executive (Council of Ministers) is responsible to the legislature
Ministers cannot be members of the legislature

questions.stem: Which of the following are “unitary” features that make the Indian Constitution quasi-federal?
subs: 1. Residuary powers are vested in the Union.
2. Single citizenship and an integrated judiciary.
3. Parliament can alter the area, boundaries or name of a state without its consent.

questions.stem: The doctrine of the “Basic Structure” of the Constitution — that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure — was propounded in which case?
Which of the following terms were added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by the Constitutional (42nd) Amendment, 1976?
subs: 1. Socialist
2. Secular
3. Integrity
4. Fraternity

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Preamble of the Indian Constitution:
subs: 1. It is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru.
2. It is enforceable in a court of law.

questions.stem: Match List I (Feature borrowed) with List II (Source Constitution) and select the correct answer:
subs: A. Directive Principles of State Policy 1. British Constitution
B. Fundamental Rights and judicial review 2. Irish Constitution
C. Parliamentary form and rule of law 3. Canadian Constitution
D. Federation with a strong centre; residuary powers with the centre 4. US Constitution

questions.stem: The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution of India pertains to the administration of tribal areas in which of the following States?
options: Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the distribution of legislative powers under the Seventh Schedule:
subs: 1. The residuary power to legislate on subjects not enumerated in any of the three Lists rests with the State Legislatures.
2. If a law made by Parliament and a law made by a State on a Concurrent-List subject conflict, the law made by Parliament prevails.

questions.stem: Which one of the following languages was added to the Eighth Schedule by a Constitutional Amendment in 1967?
Consider the following statements:
subs: 1. Article 1 describes India as a “Union of States.”
2. Under Article 3, Parliament can form a new state or alter the area, boundaries or name of an existing state.

questions.stem: With reference to Articles 2 and 3, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Article 2 deals with the reorganisation of existing states, while Article 3 deals with admission of new states
A bill under Article 3 requires the prior recommendation of the President and reference to the concerned state legislature
A bill under Article 3 needs the consent (not merely opinion) of the concerned state legislature
Article 3 requires ratification by half of the state legislatures

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about constitutional amendments requiring ratification by the states:
subs: 1. An amendment affecting the powers of the Supreme Court and the High Courts requires ratification by the legislatures of not less than half of the states.
2. An amendment to Article 368 itself also requires such ratification by the states.

questions.stem: With reference to the reorganisation of states, consider the following statements:
subs: 1. Andhra State, created in 1953, was the first state formed on a linguistic basis.
2. The Fazl Ali Commission accepted language as a basis for reorganisation but rejected the theory of “one language, one state.”

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of Indian federalism?
options: The federating units consented to form a union
Residuary powers vest with the Centre
An extensive Union and Concurrent List

questions.stem: Consider the following statements relating to Article 13:
subs: 1. A constitutional amendment is not treated as “law” under Article 13, though it can be struck down if it violates the basic structure.
2. Under the doctrine of severability, only the part of a law that is inconsistent with Fundamental Rights is struck down, while the rest survives if it can operate independently.

questions.stem: Which of the following Fundamental Rights, as enshrined in the Constitution, belong only to citizens (and not to foreigners)?
subs: 1. Article 19 – Protection of the right to freedom of speech
2. Article 21 – Protection of life and personal liberty
3. Article 15 – Prohibition of discrimination
4. Article 16 – Equality of opportunity in public employment

questions.stem: Which one of the following is an exception to the “equality before law” guaranteed under Article 14?
options: The President of India and State Governors (Article 361)

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency:
subs: 1. During a National Emergency, all the Fundamental Rights stand automatically suspended.
2. Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended, even during a National Emergency.

questions.stem: The Right to Privacy was declared a Fundamental Right (a facet of Article 21) by the Supreme Court in which case?
options: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)

questions.stem: According to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, which one of the following Articles is the “heart and soul” of the Constitution of India?
Consider the following statements regarding the writ of Mandamus:
subs: 1. It can be issued to compel a public authority to perform a public duty that it has failed to discharge.
2. It can be issued against the President of India and the Governors of states.

questions.stem: Which one of the following writs is issued by the Supreme Court to secure the freedom of a person upon unlawful arrest or detention?
Which among the following writs is issued to quash the order of a court or tribunal?
Consider the following statements regarding the rights of an arrested person under Article 22 (ordinary law):
subs: 1. The person must be produced before the nearest Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest, excluding the time needed for the journey.
2. The person has the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his or her choice.

questions.stem: Which one of the following Directive Principles of State Policy is classified as a “Gandhian” principle?
options: Organising village panchayats as units of self-government (Article 40)

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) is correct?
options: They are enforceable in courts like Fundamental Rights
They are non-justiciable but fundamental in governance, aiming at social and economic democracy
They are individual-centric, unlike the community-centric Fundamental Rights
They were borrowed from the US Constitution

questions.stem: According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, which one of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
options: To provide education to one's child
To promote village and cottage industries

questions.stem: Which one of the following was added as a Fundamental Duty through the Constitution (86th Amendment) Act, 2002?
options: To strive towards excellence in individual and collective activity
To provide opportunities for education to one's child between the ages of 6 and 14 years
To work for the welfare of women and children

questions.stem: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of which committee?
Which one of the following is NOT included in the electoral college that elects the President of India?
options: Elected members of the Lok Sabha
Elected members of the state Legislative Assemblies
Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry

questions.stem: Which one of the following methods is followed in electing the President of India?
options: Proportional Representation and the Single Transferable Vote System
Proportional Representation and the First-Past-the-Post System

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the impeachment of the President under Article 61:
subs: 1. The sole ground for impeachment is “violation of the Constitution.”
2. Both elected and nominated members of Parliament take part in the impeachment, but members of state legislatures do not.

questions.stem: With reference to the pardoning power of the Governor under Article 161, which one of the following is correct?
options: The Governor can pardon a death sentence
The Governor can pardon a sentence awarded by a court martial
The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence but can suspend, remit or commute it
The Governor has no power of pardon in any case

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the office of the Governor of a state:
subs: 1. The Governor is directly elected by the people of the state.
2. The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:
options: Members of the Lok Sabha only
Members of both Houses of Parliament (both elected and nominated)
Members of both Houses of Parliament and the state Legislative Assemblies
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament only

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India (Article 76):
subs: 1. He is appointed by the President of India.
2. He is not debarred from private legal practice.

questions.stem: The total number of members in the Union Council of Ministers in India shall not exceed:
options: 10% of the total number of members of Parliament
15% of the total number of members of Parliament
10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha

questions.stem: The twelve members nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha are chosen for their special knowledge or practical experience in:
options: Literature, science, art and social service

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Anti-Defection Law:
subs: 1. It was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment.
2. A question of disqualification on the ground of defection is decided by the President.

questions.stem: Any question pertaining to the disqualification of a member of the Lok Sabha on the ground of defection is decided by:
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.stem: Whether a particular bill is a Money Bill or not is finally decided by:
options: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, whose decision is final

questions.stem: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha can be held up (delayed) by the Rajya Sabha for a maximum of how many weeks?
Consider the following statements about a No-Confidence Motion:
subs: 1. It can be moved in either House of Parliament.
2. If it is passed, the entire Council of Ministers must resign.

questions.stem: A motion of no-confidence is moved against:
Consider the following statements about the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament:
subs: 1. It has 22 members drawn from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
2. By convention, its Chairman is appointed from the Opposition.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about a Judge of the Supreme Court of India is correct?
options: A Supreme Court judge retires on attaining the age of 62 years
A Supreme Court judge is appointed by the Chief Justice of India
A retired Supreme Court judge may plead before any court in India
A Supreme Court judge holds office until 65 years of age and is appointed by the President through the collegium system

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a qualification required for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court?
options: At least five years as a Judge of a High Court
At least ten years as an Advocate of a High Court
In the opinion of the President, a distinguished jurist
At least twenty years as a Sub-Judicial Magistrate

questions.stem: The power of the Supreme Court to decide a dispute between two or more States is called:
The judgment of the Supreme Court of India in the Vishakha case pertains to:
options: Sexual harassment of women at the workplace

questions.stem: A Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court can be removed:
options: By the President at his own discretion
By a simple majority of Parliament
By the President, after an address by each House of Parliament passed by a special majority, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity

questions.stem: A National Emergency under Article 352 can be proclaimed on which of the following grounds?
subs: 1. War
2. External aggression
3. Armed rebellion

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding Articles 358 and 359:
subs: 1. Under Article 359, the six freedoms of Article 19 are automatically suspended the moment a National Emergency is proclaimed.
2. Under Article 358, Article 19 is automatically suspended during an emergency declared on the ground of war or external aggression.

questions.stem: President's Rule imposed in a state under Article 356 can be extended to a maximum period of:
options: Three years (with parliamentary approval every six months)

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about a Financial Emergency (Article 360) is correct?
options: It has never been proclaimed in India so far
It has been declared once, during the crisis of 1991
It is declared on the ground of armed rebellion
It requires fresh parliamentary approval every six months

questions.stem: Which one of the following States does NOT have a Legislative Council?
Which of the following statements regarding the Indian federal system is/are correct?
subs: 1. All States have equal representation in the Rajya Sabha.
2. Consent of a State is not required for altering its boundaries.
3. There is no dual citizenship in India.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the 73rd Amendment (Panchayati Raj):
subs: 1. It added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.
2. The minimum age to contest a panchayat election is 21 years.
3. Not less than one-third of the seats are reserved for women at all three tiers.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a STATUTORY body (created by an Act of Parliament), and not a constitutional body?
Which one of the following statements about the Election Commission of India is correct?
options: It is established under Article 324, and the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court
It conducts elections to the panchayats and municipalities as well
The Chief Election Commissioner holds office during the pleasure of the President and can be removed at any time
It consists only of the Chief Election Commissioner, with no other members
